title: Babylon
summary: The imperial city that becomes a biblical symbol of exile, judgment, and arrogant worldly power.
historical_context: Babylon was the Neo-Babylonian imperial center that destroyed Jerusalem and sent Judah into exile.
ancient_near_east_context: As a major Mesopotamian power, Babylon represents empire, monumentality, and the temptation to trust human glory rather than covenant faithfulness.
literary_context: The city appears in exile narratives and prophetic critique, then reappears in Revelation as a symbol of idolatrous power.
covenantal_significance: Babylon embodies the covenant consequences of rebellion while also highlighting God's power to judge empire and restore his people.
interpretive_notes: Distinguish historical Babylon from symbolic Babylon in Revelation.
The city's theological load in Scripture is bound up with exile, arrogance, and divine judgment.
common_questions: Why is Babylon important in the Bible?
